observed_original_abi.calling_convention: __thiscall, receiver in ECX, zero stack arguments, callee pops nothing
observed_original_abi.calling_convention_evidence: the body names no memory operand at all, so there is no entry slot from which an argument could be read; the terminator at 0x00e31102 is a bare RET (`c3`) with no immediate, so the callee pops nothing; the address is a slot value of a vptr-backed vftable (508 tables in .spore-analysis/ghidra-exports/vtables.json), so it is a non-static virtual member function and therefore has a receiver, which on x86-32 MSVC can only arrive in a register. Of __thiscall/__fastcall only ECX carries it, and __fastcall is removed because EDX is never read either. ECX itself is never read in any form, so the receiver parameter is unnamed in the source.
observed_original_abi.calling_convention_alternatives: __cdecl and __stdcall are excluded: both require at least one argument on the stack, and this body consumes none. __fastcall is not separable from __thiscall on this body (a single-ECX-argument fastcall and a __thiscall place the same pointer in ECX, and ECX is never read either way). The receiver framing rests on the vftable-slot evidence, not on the three bytes alone.
observed_original_abi.receiver: ECX, never read: the complete two-instruction body contains no reference to ECX in any form
observed_original_abi.receiver_disposition: bounds_only and EMPTY. The machine-derived receiver record carries register=ECX with offsets=[] and distinct_offsets=0, which is the same shape as the shared default stub at 0x00b1e4d0. No displacement, no extent and no member of any receiver type is claimed, and none is derivable: the body names no memory operand.
observed_original_abi.stack_arguments_evidence: the two-instruction body contains no ESP-relative operand of any kind, so there is no entry slot to read
observed_original_abi.return_semantics: EAX holds zero at the RET: XOR EAX,EAX at 0x00e31100 is the last and only write to EAX and nothing overwrites it before the terminator. The operand is the FULL 32-bit register, so all four bytes are written and none of them is indeterminate. The derived ABI record reports return_register EAX, return_semantics integral_in_EAX and register_class integral.
observed_original_abi.return_type_caveat: The declared width is the width the machine writes (four bytes, from the full-register operand), which is a stronger statement than the ABI record alone carries. Whether the ORIGINAL source spelled it int, unsigned, an iterator typedef or a bool-with-a-wide-return is NOT established: several spellings compile to these same three bytes. The package declares std::int32_t because that is the value EAX provably carries and because src/reconstruction/pkg08_cell_mode already consumes this call site as a std::int32_t (its OpaqueIterator), seeding a four-byte local cursor word with the result.
observed_original_abi.relationship_to_promoted_code: src/reconstruction/pkg08_cell_mode/mode_on_exit.hpp declares `using IteratorBegin00e31100 = OpaqueIterator (*)();`, a zero-argument function pointer. That is the same machine call with the dead ECX register dropped, not a competing claim: the body reads ECX in no form, so whether the caller sets ECX is unobservable at this entry. Both spellings are recorded in the package header (AbiSharedZeroResult00e31100 and AbiIteratorBegin00e31100) and the model test runs both trampolines against this entry and against a nonzero reference, proving they agree here. pkg08's own metadata for its call site records the same facts: ECX = dword[0x016b3c04] + 0x54, no ordinary stack arguments, return EAX = 0.

verification.byte_identity: NOT byte-identical, and this is stated rather than claimed. The binary bytes are 33 c0 c3 (opcode 33 /r, the reg,reg form of XOR). Both clang++ and g++ at -m32 -O1/-O2/-Os emit 31 c0 c3 (opcode 31 /r, the r/m,reg form) for the same body - the same operation on the same register through the other direction encoding, three bytes, identical machine semantics, different opcode byte. No available compiler on this machine reproduces the 33 form, so no byte-identity claim is made and the encoding is pinned instead by kTargetBytes in the header with static_asserts, which the mutation harness exercises.
verification.mutation_test: 12 of 12 mutations refuted: 6 by a runtime diagnostic in the model test, 6 by a compile-time static_assert in the package. Baseline passes. The harness deletes the archive before every link and uses `ar rc`, never `ar qc`, and compiles the test from the MUTATED directory so header mutations are actually exercised. Two holes were found and closed during this run: M6 originally tried to narrow the return at the source level, which is unobservable because a C++ body that returns 0 compiles identically to one that conceptually wrote a zero byte - it was replaced by a vtable-dispatcher mutation; and H5 originally mutated the AbiSharedZeroResult00e31100 typedef rather than the entry declaration, which was NOT REFUTED because the header then asserted only sizeof(std::int32_t) == 4 - the header now measures the entry's own return width off decltype of an unevaluated call.
